narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate the severe surge in daily COVID-19 deaths in India during the second wave in early 2021.

units.meaning: The plotted series is the 7-day moving average of daily COVID-19 deaths, not cumulative deaths, cases, or another metric.

basis.note: first plotted point; establishes the series starts low

accepted_routes: daily deaths on a 7-day moving average
daily death toll smoothed over seven days
units.visual_evidence_rule: The series label or annotation must identify the line as daily deaths on a 7-day moving average.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'daily COVID-19 deaths' or 'second wave of COVID-19' clause
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly identify the measure as daily deaths 7dma rather than cases or cumulative deaths?

units.meaning: Through early 2021 the 7dma remains low and relatively flat, then turns sharply upward in April 2021 and keeps rising to the final point.

basis.note: early-2021 level before the second-wave surge
start of the steep April rise

accepted_routes: low plateau through early 2021 then steep rise
relatively flat before April 2021, then explosive increase
slow early-2021 levels followed by a sharp upward turn in April
units.visual_evidence_rule: The plotted series must visibly remain near its early-2021 values and then turn sharply upward toward the final point.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show the flat-then-steep shape of the early-2021 series, or is the peak alone sufficient?

units.meaning: From the pre-surge low around late Feb/early Mar 2021 to the final peak, daily deaths 7dma increased roughly 24-fold, or by about 3,100 daily deaths on the 7-day average.

basis.note: lowest nearby value after the Feb 2021 label; x_value blank on this row

accepted_routes: about 23–24 times higher than the pre-surge low
rose by about 3,100 daily deaths on the 7-day average
units.visual_evidence_rule: The end of the series must appear dramatically higher than the pre-surge trough, supporting a roughly 24-fold rise.
units.temporal_anchor: the 'added avoidable deaths' or 'second wave' clause
units.reviewer_question: Must the video quantify the magnitude of the surge, or is the visual steepness enough?

units.meaning: The final second-wave peak is about 2.7 times the earlier first-wave peak around September 2020.

basis.note: first-wave peak value around the Sep 2020 label

accepted_routes: nearly three times the earlier peak
roughly 2,000 more daily deaths than the first-wave peak
units.visual_evidence_rule: The final peak must be visibly much taller than the previous first-wave hump.
units.reviewer_question: Is comparing the second-wave peak to the first-wave peak required, or optional context?

units.meaning: The maximum value of the series is 3233.9229 at the final plotted point, the highest daily-deaths 7dma value in the dataset.
accepted_routes: peak reaches about 3,234 on the 7-day average
series tops out at roughly 3.2 thousand
units.visual_evidence_rule: The line must visibly reach its highest point at the end of the plotted period.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly state or label the peak value, or is the maximum implied by the curve?

optional_valid: Optional: annotate the first-wave peak around Sep 2020 for context.
Optional: call out the pre-surge low around late Feb/early Mar 2021 before the rise.
Optional: emphasize the final peak value on-screen.
unsupported_to_avoid: causal claims about demand mismatch or avoidable deaths
total COVID-19 deaths or cumulative deaths
percentages or per-capita rates not in the table
exact dates not present in x_value labels
notes: All cited numbers are from the value column for entity 'daily deaths 7dma'; ratios and differences are arithmetic combinations of those cells. The table has absolute values, so absolute daily-death counts are allowed, but causes and non-table metrics should be avoided.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
